Maps of King Grain Dam

The maps are copies of the original aerial photos which are on file at the RC Soil and Water Conservation Office and the RC Agricultural Stabilization and Conservation Service Office in Faribault, MN.

These photos show all the areas of water, including all shoreline that was created by the King Mill Dam on the Cannon River at Faribault. Acquiring the flowage rights for the land was started in 1855. The original dam and power plant was built between 1855-1885. The power plant had been in operation until 8/28/1974. The dam is in operation at the present time (12/26/1975).

Please note that the area in red is the dam site. The lakes of Cannon and Wells and the Cannon Mill Pond were formed by the building of the King Mill Dam. The King Mill Dam has had an influence on the width of the Cannon River and has influence on water levels of other lakes in the general area.

The King Mill Dam provides suggicient water in the Cannon River so one can have continuous canoeing as far south as Blue Earth. There is a long-established Marina on the Cannon Mill Pond. Hiking trails have been established along the scenic Cannon River, Cannon Lake, Wells Lake and the Cannon Mill Pond. The County of Rice has purchased the Shager Park for the residents of Rice County.

notes:
"Nineteenth-century Plains Indian drawings have often been called ledger drawings because they were made with pencil, ink, and watercolor on pages of old ledger or account books. When young Plains warriors learned to draw in this new style, the pictures they made were incorporated into the war-honors system of Plains life. The men then memorialized their deeds in pictures that they used with their oral recollections of bravery and battle, victory and loss.

"Some of the best-known ledger art was created at Fort Marion, in Saint Augustine, Florida. Between 1875 and 1878, seventy-two Cheyenne, Kiowa, Comanche, Arapaho, and Caddo men were imprisoned there because of their involvements in events connected to the Red River Wars in Indian Territory (later Oklahoma). Encouraged to draw by their military captors, twenty-six of the prisoners, mostly Cheyenne and Kiowa, produced hundreds of drawings and a number of books detailing their former lives as warriors, hunters, and suitors as well as their new lives as prisoners and students."

(Source: Smitsonian, http://americanhistory.si.edu/documentsgallery/exhibitions/ledger_drawing_2.html)

Swedish letter.

descrip:
Swedish letter.

According to Jared Morningstar, a Gustavus professor, this is "A letter addressed to the writer's brother - presumably Axel - July 13th, 1870.  The letter focuses on giving him updates regarding the lives of friends and family and asking for news from Axel.  One man moved to Chicago where there are many Swedes, but he is in debt and will need to sell some of his clothes and save his salary in order to survive."

The pieces are not numbered.
title: Letter from Axel's brother to Axel

title: Letter from Lena Ulin to Axel Ulin

descrip:
Loose items removed from field books (2019.268.007-030) and the boxes that the field books and linen longitudinal profiles (2019.268.031-096) came in upon accession. These items were removed at time of cataloging and put in folders by the object they were found in. SG and LS then went through these folders and seperated out items to put in their own folder based on uniqueness and the items' condition. Any folders after an "Items Removed From Book ..." folder contain items from that books. For example, the items in folders ai and aj came from the same book as the items in folder ah. This is explicitly stated on the folders themselves, but not in the container list titles.

Items range from pieces of paper used as scratch paper for surveyor's calculations or bookmarks, to letters, newspaper clippings, info on local campaigns, maps, longitudinal profiles, sketches of plots, documents related to inssurance, bee keeping packets, bank slips, etc. We priotritized scratch paper with calculations if the paper itself was of historical value, or if words or a sketch were included with the calculations. The dates of the objects do not necessarily reflect the dates of the entries in the books - it is unclear why.

Scope and Contents:
The contents of the Friends of Buckham Library collection are divided into two boxes. Box One includes By-Laws, Non-Profit Corp. Conflict of Interest, Secretary Minutes (1961-1984), Quarterly Annual Meetings and Reports (1990-2016), Breakfast Fundraiser (2009-2016), Whillock Carving Project, Library Rededication, Photos of Sponsored Events, Friends Correspondence, and Newspaper Articles of Sponsored Events. 
Box Two includes Bank Statements (1992-2015), Library Taxes (1987-2013), Tax Exemption Correspondence (1991-2002), Library Invoices (2001-2016), Treasurers Reports (1991-2015), Alliance Bernstein Investments, Grants, CAB Funds, Vanguard Charitable Endowment Program, Mary Carey Memorial, and Friends of the Library Deposit Records. 
Both boxes show the developmental history of the program, how it started, and how it evolved to what it is today. 

Historical Note:

The Friends of the Library began on February 5, 1961. Dr. C.F. Robertshaw was president with Marion Cook as secretary. Meetings were held at the library and after the first year, meetings were held annually. To be a member of Friends of the Library, there were two options. To be a guarantor member, the contributor would give $5 or more per year. To have the sustaining membership, the minimum contribution was $1. The group provided ideas for various programs the Library could initiate, holidays that could be celebrated for the Library, and how the Library could improve. The Friends of the Library provided numerous events such as, a Breakfast Fundraiser, different speakers from various places, musical events (such as some of the Orchestra from St. Olaf), and events for school age children. The organization still continues today, creating programs and engaging in the community.

notes: The Faribault Rifle and Pistol Club was started in the 1940s.  The pistol group shot in the "old gym" in the 1914 high school until the school was closed. Then they shot at Shattuck, later at Lockerby's and finally at the new range club house.  C.E. Purdie started a Jr. Rifle Club in the late 1940s who shot in the same gym.  LeRoy Rockman remembers shooting at the school during an Activity Period in 1956 & '57.  FRPC had active big bore & small bore rifle groups as well as small bore pistol for many years.  Later combat pistol became popular.
